claim: At Aurora's scale (<=1 TB stored, high scenario) the chosen platform serves retention dashboards at p95 < 5 s within its compute allocation.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Public benchmarks run TPC-DS at 1-100 TB with tuned configs and list prices; Aurora's query mix, concurrency and negotiated pricing are unique.
test_method: Build the 3 core retention marts on synthetic data sized to the high scenario on 2 shortlisted platforms; replay 2 weeks of dashboard query logs; record p95 latency, credits/DBUs and stored bytes.
pass_threshold: p95 < 5 s at 20 concurrent users; projected compute <= 50% of A-BUD-01 base; measured compression within A-STO-01 range

claim: The ML team can pull a 12-month churn feature set into training without a manual export copy.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Depends on Aurora's ML stack (notebooks, feature store, connectors) and network/egress setup.
test_method: From each shortlisted platform, read the feature table into the ML team's training environment via native connector or open table format; time the extract and check schema/point-in-time correctness.
pass_threshold: Full 12-month extract < 15 min; zero row-count or point-in-time mismatches vs source

claim: The chosen orchestrator can backfill 12 months of models and features within an 8-hour overnight window.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Backfill time depends on Aurora's DAG size, partitioning and warehouse concurrency, not on the orchestrator alone.
test_method: Run a full 12-month backfill of staging -> marts -> features on high-scenario synthetic data under each shortlisted orchestrator.
pass_threshold: Backfill completes < 8 h with no manual restarts

claim: Asset/lineage-aware orchestration catches data-quality faults before retention-team consumers see them.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Detection depends on Aurora's specific tests, freshness SLAs and failure modes.
test_method: Seed 20 representative faults (late billing webhook, duplicated events, schema drift, null churn labels) and measure detection point and time.
pass_threshold: >= 90% of seeded faults blocked before mart publish; median detection < 30 min

claim: A single analytics engineer can add a new model with tests and ownership metadata in under one working day.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Team skill mix and local conventions dominate; surveys report averages across very different teams.
test_method: Time-box onboarding exercise: two engineers each add one new mart + tests on each shortlisted orchestrator.
pass_threshold: Median < 1 working day; no platform-team assistance required

claim: Retention interventions do not need data fresher than 15 minutes to change outcomes.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Value of freshness depends on Aurora customer behavior and the retention team's intervention playbook; no external study covers it.
test_method: From historical data, measure the lag between first churn signal (cancel-page visit, skip, failed payment) and the cancellation event; review intervention response times with the retention team.
pass_threshold: Median signal-to-cancel lag > 1 h and retention team cannot act faster than 15 min => micro-batch accepted

claim: Micro-batch at 15-minute cadence absorbs high-scenario peak-day load within the ingestion budget.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Burst shape on Aurora promo days and per-batch platform cost are workload-specific.
test_method: Replay last BFCM clickstream scaled to the high scenario (~37.6M events/day) through the micro-batch pipeline; record end-to-end lag and cost.
pass_threshold: p95 end-to-end lag < 20 min on peak day; ingestion spend <= A-BUD-02 ingestion allocation

claim: Retrieval over Aurora transcripts finds the right supporting passages for retention-agent questions.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Domain language, transcript quality and chunking interact; general embedding benchmarks do not predict Aurora recall.
test_method: Label 200 real retention-agent questions with gold transcript passages; compare chunk sizes and 2-3 embedding models.

claim: The assistant's answers stay grounded in Aurora policy and transcripts and never leak PII.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Hallucination and PII risk depend on Aurora's policies, redaction pipeline and red-team prompts.
test_method: Run RAGAS-style faithfulness scoring plus a 150-prompt red-team set (policy invention, refund promises, PII extraction) against the assistant.
pass_threshold: Faithfulness >= 0.95; unsupported policy statements < 1%; PII redaction recall >= 99%

claim: A tool-using agent improves retention-task success enough over a fixed RAG workflow to justify its extra cost and variance.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Agent gains reported on public benchmarks are task-specific and often ignore cost and run-to-run reliability.
test_method: Run both designs on the same 200-task eval set (look up account, explain options, propose offer) with k=4 repeated trials each.
pass_threshold: Adopt agentic only if task success +10 pts and pass^4 not lower than workflow at <= 2x cost

claim: Cost per assistant conversation stays at or below the A-BUD-03 base value at acceptable latency.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Token usage per conversation depends on Aurora's transcripts, prompts and model choice; vendor price sheets give rates, not usage.
test_method: Two-week pilot with 10 retention agents; log tokens, cache hits, latency and cost per conversation.
pass_threshold: Mean cost <= $0.05 per conversation; p95 latency <= 4 s

claim: Human reviewers reliably catch the plausible-but-wrong bugs that agent-authored transformation PRs introduce.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Depends on Aurora's reviewers, review load, dbt project and policy tests; public agent benchmarks use Python issues, not SQL with incremental semantics.
test_method: 4-week shadow pilot on synthetic subscription data: agent opens PRs; 5 seeded bugs (late-event double-count, new subscription_status level, PII column exposure, PK change, broken point-in-time join) are hidden among routine PRs; track catch rate and review minutes.
pass_threshold: >= 4 of 5 seeded bugs caught before staging merge; added review time <= 4 h per engineer per week

claim: Planning placeholders for churn, engagement and transcript length are within the register's low-high ranges.
why_not_externally_sourceable: These are Aurora's own operating metrics; industry figures are only placeholders.
test_method: Pull trailing-12-month cohort churn (billing), 30-day DAU and events/session (product analytics), and token length of a 1,000-transcript sample (helpdesk).
pass_threshold: Each measured value falls within low-high; otherwise update register and re-run projections

claim: Component spend tracks the A-BUD-02 allocation and the total stays under the A-BUD-01 ceiling.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Only Aurora's tagged cloud bill shows actual spend by component.
test_method: Tag all data-platform resources by component; review 90 days of billing against allocation.
pass_threshold: No component > 125% of its allocation; total run-rate <= A-BUD-01 base

claim: Late-arriving events fall within the register's reprocessing window.
why_not_externally_sourceable: Arrival lag depends on Aurora's apps, payment processor and webhook providers.
test_method: Compute the distribution of ingested_at minus event_time over 30 days of events by source.
pass_threshold: p99 lag <= A-OPS-03 base (3 days); otherwise widen the incremental lookback
